<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's official GitHub repository using a versioned tarball URL: `$pkgname-$pkgver.tar.gz::$url/archive/v$pkgver.tar.gz`. The checksum is explicitly provided using sha256sums, so the source integrity will be verified during normal makepkg execution (though as per policy, even a 'SKIP' would not make this unsafe for the current narrow gate).

During the sourcing phase (which includes evaluation of global variables and the `pkgver()` function, if present), no command substitution or external code execution occurs. There are no top-level commands, backticks, `$(...)`, or function definitions outside of the known lifecycle functions. The `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, and `package()` functions are defined but will not be executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags, so their contents are out of scope for this narrow safety gate.

All operations in the global scope are harmless variable assignments. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or any other malicious behavior that could be triggered during sourcing or source fetching.
</details>

No dangerous code in sourcing or source fetch phase</summary>
